criteria.criterion: Run cargo test. A positive end-to-end test passes: a result event whose top-level usage differs from modelUsage (main thread plus subagent on the requested model) goes through parsing, the invocation record and check_invocation with no Reconciliation violation.
criteria.evidence: a_result_whose_top_level_usage_includes_a_subagent_reconciles_end_to_end passed. Its AGREEING event has top-level usage 90/134508/3634696/52656, and the sonnet modelUsage is 6/3821/275219/3136. The event goes through StreamState::on_line, then output_from_result (the same function the real driver now calls), then Athena::invocation_record. The test asserts the record's tokens equal the modelUsage figures and that check_invocation returns no violations. On the base, output used result.usage. That would record 90/… and trip the token-mismatch branch, so this test would fail without the fix.

criteria.criterion: Run cargo test. A named negative end-to-end test, a_result_whose_totals_disagree_with_model_usage_is_flagged_end_to_end, builds the record from a result event that has modelUsage for the requested model and really disagrees with it. It uses the same parse-and-record path as the positive test and does not edit the record by hand. It asserts check_invocation returns a Reconciliation violation.
criteria.evidence: The test passed. It uses the same record_from helper (parse, then output_from_result, then invocation_record) and never edits the record. The DISAGREEING event has sonnet modelUsage, and its total_cost_usd of 0.75 disagrees with the per-model costs (0.10 + 0.20). The test asserts exactly one Reconciliation violation whose detail contains 'per-model costs sum'. The disagreement is in cost, which the accepted reading allows ('a cost disagreement is an alternative for the negative case'). Under the new definition a token disagreement cannot reach a record except through the fallback, which criterion 3 rules out. Removing the cost check would leave zero violations and the test would fail; I reasoned this from reconcile.rs lines 66-76 and did not run it.

criteria.criterion: Before calling check_invocation, the negative test asserts that the built record's totals differ from the modelUsage sum. Its event is not one with no modelUsage, so it does not reach the 'no usage for the requested model' branch.
criteria.evidence: Before calling check_invocation, the test asserts record.models_used.contains_key(MODEL) and that |record.cost - sum(models_used.cost_usd)| > 0.01. Its event carries modelUsage for claude-sonnet-5-5, so the 'no usage' branch is not reached. The test also asserts the single violation is the cost one.

criteria.criterion: The invocation's measured tokens and the gate's reconciliation rule use one definition of what an invocation used (modelUsage). The code or the CHANGELOG states it. The legacy exception is either removed or limited to older records.
criteria.evidence: ResultEvent::requested_usage (stream.rs) returns models_used[model], and output_from_result (claude.rs) uses it for AgentOutput.usage. The gate (reconcile.rs lines 84-99) compares models_used[inv.model] with the tokens. The invocation.rs module doc and the CHANGELOG 'Fixed' entry both state the one definition, and the measured_basis text changed to 'result.modelUsage for the requested model'. A grep for 'legacy' in crates/ finds no exception in the gate, which matches the CHANGELOG's statement that there was none to remove.

criteria.criterion: Run cargo clippy --all-targets and cargo fmt --check. Both are clean, and the full cargo test passes.
criteria.evidence: Clippy finished with no warnings, fmt --check was silent, and every cargo test suite reported ok with 0 failed (athena-core: 192 passed, 1 ignored).

criteria.criterion: The final report maps each criterion to a named test or command output.
criteria.evidence: This verdict maps each criterion to a named test or command, and the CHANGELOG names both end-to-end tests. The producer's own report is not in my snapshot, so I could not check its table directly.

findings.summary: The negative test's disagreement is in cost, not tokens. Its top-level usage equals the modelUsage token sum.
findings.evidence: In DISAGREEING, top-level usage 90/134508/3634696/52656 equals sonnet plus haiku modelUsage exactly. Only total_cost_usd (0.75 vs 0.30) disagrees. The proposal asked for an event whose top-level usage totals differ from the modelUsage sum. The accepted reading allows a cost disagreement, and under the new definition top-level usage no longer reaches the record, so this is the meaningful negative case. A reader of the proposal may still expect a token-level case.

findings.summary: There is no unit test for the fallback in requested_usage (no modelUsage entry for the requested model).
findings.evidence: The None => self.usage branch is not exercised by any new test. Records built through it would still be flagged by the gate's 'no usage for the requested model' branch, as on the base, so this is not a regression.

findings.summary: Three expected deliverables were left unchanged: fake.rs, reconcile.rs and landing_tests.rs.
findings.evidence: The diff touches only CHANGELOG.md, claude.rs, stream.rs and invocation.rs, all of which are on the list. No file outside the list changed, so there is no scope finding.

summary: The change gives an invocation's recorded tokens the same meaning the gate checks: the requested model's modelUsage. It adds ResultEvent::requested_usage, which top-level usage backs up only when modelUsage has no entry for the model, and output_from_result, which the real Claude driver now calls. That fixes the root cause where it starts, not in the gate. Two new end-to-end tests in athena-core run a result event through stream parsing, output_from_result, invocation_record and check_invocation. The positive test has a subagent, so top-level usage differs from modelUsage, and it reconciles cleanly; it would fail on the base. The named negative test builds its record from a real event through the same path. Before the check it asserts the reported cost differs from the per-model sum and that modelUsage for the requested model is present, then it asserts exactly one cost Reconciliation violation. The disagreement is in cost rather than tokens, which the accepted reading allows. Under the new definition a token disagreement cannot reach a record except through the fallback. I ran the two tests, clippy with -D warnings, fmt --check and the full cargo test, and all are clean. The changed files are all on the deliverables list. My findings are minor only: the negative case uses cost rather than tokens, and the fallback branch has no unit test.
